newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada grants three LMCS communications licenses.
newsitem.headline: Canada grants three LMCS communications licenses.

text.p: Canada granted three licenses on Tuesday for the new high-speed wireless communications technology LMCS that will compete with cable and telephone companies.

However, Industry Minister John Manley said cable and phone companies would be able to bid in two years in the next round of licenses, which will at that time be auctioned off. There was no auction in the first round.
The three winners are Cellular Vision, Regional Vision and Digital Vision. Applicant Fonorola Inc and 10 other companies were not in the list of winners.
Cellular Vision Canada Ltd is wholly owned by WIC Western International Communications Ltd.

Digital Vision, which since its application has been renamed MaxLink, was 12 percent held at the time of application by Texas Instruments Inc. It has a number of other private shareholders, including MaxLink President Joel Bell. The Quebec government's Caisse de Depot's communications investment arm is another shareholder.
Regional Vision is 49 percent owned by Canadian Satellite Communications Inc and 29 percent by a joint venture of SNC-Lavalin Group Inc and Bracknell Corp.

LMCS stands for local multipoint communications systems, a broadband telecommunications service that can provide wireless digital television channels, CD quality sound, high-speed Internet access and video teleconferencing.
Signals from a central transmitting/receiving station will be sent to and received from home and businesses within a 4-5 km (2-3 mile) radius, requiring several stations in each city.
In addition to the spectrum licenses awarded by Manley to LMCS operators, those seeking to distribute broadcast programming via LMCS will also require a broadcast distribution license.

The frequency band for LMCS consists of six spectrum blocks of 500 megahertz each. Two of these are being made available immediately to Tuesday's winners, which Manley said should inaugurate service in 12-24 months.
Two of the four remaining frequency blocks will be auctioned 24 months from now.
Cellular Vision will have 33 of the 66 main urban areas, including Toronto, Edmonton, Vancouver and Quebec City.
MaxLink (Digital) will have the other 33, including Montreal, Ottawa, Windsor, Calgary, Winnipeg and and Victoria.

Regional Vision will have 127 smaller communities distributed across Canada. An official at Canadian Satellite Communications (Cancom) said this complemented Cancom's business, which has always been to provide broadcast signals to more remote communities. -- Randall Palmer, Reuters Ottawa Bureau (613) 235-6745
